--- page 3 ---
Introduction
This course pack collects short readings on memory and attention.
Each reading is followed by questions that help you check your understanding.
Read the introduction to each section before the readings themselves.
Notes
These notes explain how the readings fit together.
Some readings overlap, and the notes point out where authors disagree.
Use them as a guide, not as a replacement for the readings.
--- page 4 ---
Results
Students who used the questions after each reading scored higher on the final exam.
The benefit was largest for students who answered the questions without looking back at the text.
Students who only reread the material showed little improvement over the term.
--- page 5 ---
Discussion
Answering questions works because it forces retrieval.
Each successful retrieval makes the memory easier to find the next time.
Rereading feels productive, but it mostly builds familiarity rather than recall.
--- page 6 ---
In short, testing yourself is one of the most useful habits a student can build.
